entries.gave: Read the Cut, invoicer as it stands (command.py, lines.py, render.py, totals.py, tax.py, __init__.py, pyproject.toml 1.4.0, both test files, no .gitignore, 8 compiled files committed under __pycache__), and the four Mores kept. The people: colleagues from accounting, who save an invoice's lines from their spreadsheet and run invoicer with the client's rate to print the invoice, and the maintainers who change the package and the code that calls it.
Read code/best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-code/best-practice.md, to their end.
Took python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, the test command that pyproject.toml gives.
Ran the tests before any change in a throwaway copy: 44 tests, OK.

No architecture holds the part; the request and the Cut's decisions set it. The unit cases are the tests of tests/test_command.py, with new ones written first: test_prints_a_description_saved_in_quotes_as_typed, test_prints_a_description_holding_a_semicolon, test_refuses_a_heading_row_asking_to_leave_it_out, test_refuses_a_row_with_an_empty_description, test_skips_a_row_whose_cells_are_all_empty, and test_prints_the_subtotal_and_total_that_the_package_gives.

Decisions left to the code: how a row is split into cells (the csv module with ; as the spreadsheet writes it), how a heading row is told from a wrong row (the first row that is not blank, with neither its price nor its quantity a number), whether a row of empty cells is blank (it is, as a spreadsheet saves an empty row as ;;), and where the stated amounts are reckoned (one module).

Each decision to one module: lines.py the form of a row and its refusals, tax.py the rounding to the cent, totals.py the amounts that the invoice states (each line to the cent, subtotal, tax, total), render.py only the layout of the text, command.py the command line. No new module.
No decision has variants that a case calls for now, so no Adapter or other pattern.
Offered names: lines ROW, Line, LineError, parse_lines; tax to_cent, tax_of; totals line_amount, subtotal, tax, total; render render; command main. Everything else keeps a leading underscore.

Each planned branch named by its case: the csv reading by the quoted-cell cases, the heading branch by test_refuses_a_heading_row_asking_to_leave_it_out, the empty description by test_refuses_a_row_with_an_empty_description, skipping empty cells by test_skips_a_row_whose_cells_are_all_empty. No strict csv mode or catch of csv.Error, as no case reaches one.

Cases inside the part, supporting the command cases: in test_lines.py test_reads_a_cell_saved_in_quotes_as_typed, test_reads_a_cell_holding_a_semicolon_saved_in_quotes, test_numbers_a_row_after_a_cell_holding_a_new_row, test_skips_a_row_of_empty_cells, test_refuses_a_heading_row_naming_it, test_refuses_a_wrong_price_on_the_first_row_as_a_price, test_refuses_an_empty_description_naming_the_row; in a new test_totals.py test_states_each_line_amount_to_the_cent, test_subtotal_adds_the_amounts_as_stated, test_total_is_the_subtotal_and_the_tax_as_stated.
No case needed that supports no case of the part.
Inputs from outside: the LINES path and the --rate text, first in command.main by argparse; the saved file, opened in command.main; its text, first read into lines by lines.parse_lines.
Took python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, the test command that pyproject.toml gives.
The manifest gives a command, so no search for a runner was needed; the tests use unittest.
Ran the tests before any change in a throwaway copy: 44 tests, OK.

Things and their names: a row (text, of the saved file) and a line (Line, of the invoice); a cell/field of a row; an amount (Line.amount, unrounded) and the amount the invoice states; the rate; the subtotal, tax and total.
No architecture or README names these; the Cut says line, row, description, price, quantity, subtotal, tax, total, rate.
Field and cell name one thing in a row; the messages say field, as the code does, so field is kept.
amount named both the unrounded Line.amount and the stated one; the stated one becomes totals.line_amount, documented as to the cent, and Line.amount stays unrounded.
Rules written in more than one place: the subtotal and total, in render.py and again in totals.py; the separator and ROW only in lines.py; rounding to the cent only in tax.py.
The two subtotals must change together, as the Cut decides one figure for both, so they are one rule.
totals.py keeps the subtotal and total, as its opening says it holds the totals; render.py imports them from there, and totals.py imports only tax.py, so no import cycle.
Kinds done in many places: refusing a wrong input, reading a number, laying out a module docstring, laying out a test.

Refusals: LineError in lines.py, argparse.ArgumentTypeError in command._rate, parser.error in command.main. Numbers: Decimal with InvalidOperation caught, in lines._price and command._rate. Tests: Given/When/Then comments, one assertion of the whole result.
No style settings in pyproject.toml; each kind keeps the way the code uses: new refusals in lines.py raise LineError, a new number check reads Decimal as _price does.
One new way: rows read by csv.reader in place of str.split, as split breaks a quoted cell, the fault the Cut names; it is the only place that splits a row.

Took each decision of the Cut as it stands. Settled without asking: rows read by the csv module with ; ; a row whose cells are all empty is blank; a heading is the first non-blank row with neither its price nor its quantity a number; the stated amounts live in totals.py (line_amount, subtotal, tax, total), which render uses; pyproject.toml says what 1.5.0 changes from 1.4.0. No point left for the person.

Ran the new tests before the code: each failed for the reason its Then names (quotes kept doubled, the quoted ; split into 4 fields, ;; refused for its empty price, the heading refused for its price, the empty description printed, line_amount missing from totals). The two that pin the price message on a non-heading row passed, as they pin what the code already does.
One test for each designed case: 5 new in test_command.py, 8 new in test_lines.py, 5 in the new test_totals.py, each name a single case, no and joining two cases.
Each expected value taken from the case: Design "Pro" as typed, 37.035 half up 37.04, three stated 0.01 give 0.03, 0.0057 gives 0.01, 0.03 and 0.01 give 0.04, messages as decided.
Each test keeps its rows and expected text in its body; shared are only saved(), run_command(), row(), LINES, and in test_totals HALF_CENTS and RATE, the setup many tests share.
No loop or branch in any test.
Failure messages where the name and values leave it unsaid: the row is numbered as in the spreadsheet, on test_numbers_a_row_after_a_cell_holding_a_new_row.

Module openings: lines.py the lines and which rows give one; tax.py the rounding to the cent; totals.py the amounts that an invoice states, each to the cent, which the printed invoice and the package both take from it; render.py the layout of the invoice as text; command.py what the command takes and prints.

Changes tried on the openings alone: a new column on the printed invoice opens render.py; a rounding other than half up opens tax.py; a total with a discount on the whole invoice opens totals.py; a spreadsheet saving with commas opens lines.py; a new option opens command.py. Each names one module.

Types on each name written or changed: totals line_amount, subtotal, tax, total (Line, Sequence[Line], Decimal); lines _line, _number; render _row. render keeps its 1.4.0 signature, as the Cut leaves the currency parameter and older type hints in the records.

Docstrings state what each offered name gives and refuses: parse_lines takes quoted cells, skips rows of empty cells, refuses a heading and an empty description; totals names the rounding and Decimal(0) for no line; each changed name says Changed in 1.5.0 what 1.4.0 gave.

Checked each new test against the docstrings: quoted cells, the row numbered as the spreadsheet does across a cell of two rows of text, the heading only on the first row not blank, the empty description, the stated amounts and Decimal results are each stated.

Wrote the least code for the failing tests: csv.reader in parse_lines, the skip of empty cells, the heading and empty-description refusals in _line, line_amount and tax in totals.py with render calling them.
Ran python3 -m unittest discover -s tests in a throwaway copy: 62 tests, OK.
Read each body: no branch without a case; render no longer reckons the subtotal itself, and no csv.Error catch or strict mode was added.
pyproject.toml: Python 3.9 or later, no other package, version 1.5.0 with a comment on what changed from 1.4.0, the test command; .gitignore leaves __pycache__/ out.
Each command test saves its file in its own temporary folder, removed by addCleanup; the lines and totals tests touch no file.
The tests run no real tool outside Python.
Ran the 62 tests three times in shuffled orders, seeds 11, 22 and 33 printed: each OK.

In a throwaway copy with an empty HOME, installed the package from its setup alone into a fresh Python 3.9.25 environment: invoicer --help and an invoice ran, and the 62 tests passed there; nothing was missing from the setup.
The tests use the real modules and files in their own temporary folders; no test double.
Each test calls only offered names: command.main, parse_lines and LineError, the package Line, render, subtotal, total, and totals.line_amount and tax; none reaches a name with an underscore.
Changed bodies under unchanged interfaces (render through _row, _price through _number): the tests passed unchanged.
Each new test asserts the whole result its Then names: the full printed row or invoice, the full message, the description and stated amount as a string with its cents.
Ran coverage.py with branches over the 62 tests: 99%, every branch run; the one line no test runs is lines.py Line.__repr__.

Line.__repr__ is in 1.4.0, which callers of the package may rest on; no case of this work calls for it, and removing it would change what 1.4.0 callers get, so it stays, named here for whoever designs the cases.
No Test strategy names an interface for property-based tests, so none written.
No property-based test ran, so no failing input to weigh.
The round takes no CI mutation report; the repository CI runs only the lint job.
No mutant listed, so nothing to remove.
No mutant listed, so none marked.

No mutant listed. The heading rule is pinned both ways by tests: only the first row not blank (test_refuses_a_row_after_the_first_as_a_price_not_a_heading) and only where the quantity is not a number either (test_refuses_a_wrong_price_on_the_first_row_as_a_price).

The saved text is read into Lines in parse_lines before anything is reckoned: the row split by csv as the spreadsheet writes it, the description checked for text, the price and quantity read and bounded; nothing inside meets a raw cell.
A first row with neither price nor quantity a number is refused as a heading, not guessed away and skipped; an empty description is refused, not printed blank.
Only InvalidOperation is caught, in _number; command.main catches each file error and LineError by type; no bare except; csv.Error is not caught, as no case reaches one in csv lenient mode.

Each new message says the program, the file and row, what is wrong and what to do: invoicer: error: h.csv, row 1: a heading, as neither its price Price nor its quantity Quantity is a number; save the lines without the heading row; and row N: the description is empty; write what the line is for, as the client reads it on the invoice.
Each check is an if that raises; no assert.

Ran the command from the command line on files saved as a spreadsheet does, CRLF and a byte order mark: a heading row, an empty description, --rate 0.19 each refused with exit 2 and a message I could act on alone; quoted cells with doubled quotes and a semicolon printed as typed, rows of ;; skipped, --rate 0 printed no tax.

Searched the tests for render, subtotal, total and parse_lines before each step: render reached by the command tests; subtotal and total by no test, so test_totals.py pins them; the quoted-cell, heading and empty-cell branches of parse_lines by no test before.

The behaviours the steps reach that were untested change by the Cut (subtotal and total as stated), so their tests take the decided values rather than pinning the old ones; _row and _number keep render and _price as they were, pinned by the command and lines tests.

Steps taken one at a time: extract _row in render; extract _number from _price; move the subtotal from render to totals.subtotal; add totals.tax and have render call total; each followed by a test run.
No step renamed a name a test uses; no expected result was changed.

Ran the tests after the steps: 62 OK; no step to undo. Callers of 1.4.0 learn of each behaviour that changed from version 1.5.0 and the Changed in 1.5.0 note of render, parse_lines, subtotal and total.
No behaviour looks wrong against its name or the Cut; the subtotal and total change only as the Cut decides.
Searched each name over the repository: every function and constant is named beyond its definition, CENT only in tax.py, kept as a name the 1.4.0 package offered.
No function only passes its call on: line_amount rounds, tax reckons the subtotal it taxes, _row lays out a row.
render currency is always EUR in the repository, but render is what the package offers to callers outside it, so it stays, as the Cut also leaves it; _line first varies by call.
Each comment kept says what the code cannot: why newline= is empty, what the regular expression and limit allow; none repeats the code.

Read each new name where used: line_amount the stated amount of a line; tax the stated tax; cells the cells of a row; first whether the row is the first not blank; _number the number a text writes; _row a row of the invoice.
Each definition matches those words, so no rename.
The stated amount named line_amount in code and tests, apart from the unrounded Line.amount; no other rename needed.

One sentence each: parse_lines gives the line of each row not blank as the spreadsheet saved it; _line gives a row its line or refuses it; _number gives the number a text writes; totals each give one stated amount; render lays out the rows; each test checks its one case.
No line stopped the reading: the csv.reader over a StringIO carries its reason in a comment, and the blank-row test is one plain all().

render reckoned the amounts and laid out the rows; the reckoning went to totals, so render only lays out. _price both read and bounded a number; reading went to _number, which the heading check also needs.
No function reads a global setting; _line takes first as a parameter rather than reading state.
render had the f-string layout beside the reckoning; the layout went to _row, so each line of render is one row.
Each one-caller helper (_row, _number, _line) has a name that says what it does without its caller, so none is folded back.
Marked as odd at first reading: io.StringIO(text, newline="") in place of splitlines; the heading check only on the first row; 9 digits in _WHOLE.
The first-row reason is carried by the parameter first and _line docstring: so it may be a heading.
Comment beside the reader: newline= empty leaves a new row inside a quoted cell to csv, as its documentation asks; the 9 digits keep their comment.
Every marked line found its reason, so none is left for the person.

Corrected the comments that no longer held: parse_lines docstring (it split at each semicolon), render docstring (it reckoned the subtotal itself), totals.subtotal (unrounded sum), the module openings of render and totals.
The subtotal and total are written once, in totals.py; render imports line_amount, subtotal, tax and total from there, and the package exports the same subtotal and total.
No shared function takes a flag that picks a branch.
No module uses another module underscore name; render and totals call only what tax and lines offer.
Every place that needs a rule reads the one Python definition, so no cross-language note is needed.

New refusals raise LineError with row N: as the others do; _number reads Decimal and catches InvalidOperation as _price did; new tests follow the Given/When/Then comments and whole-result assertions of the existing ones.
command._rate keeps its own Decimal reading, as it raises argparse.ArgumentTypeError so argparse names the option; that difference was there and its docstring says why.

Made invoicer: lines.py reads rows by csv with ; (quoted cells as typed, ;; rows skipped) and refuses a heading and an empty description; totals.py states each amount to the cent with line_amount, subtotal, tax, total, which render.py uses; version 1.5.0 with Changed in 1.5.0 notes; .gitignore leaves __pycache__/ out; 18 new tests, 62 pass. Not done: the 8 committed .pyc files under invoicer/__pycache__ and tests/__pycache__ are still tracked, as removing them needs git rm, which the commands allowed to the generator do not include.

Tried in a throwaway copy as a developer installs it and accounting runs it: installed from the repository into a fresh environment, a file saved as CSV UTF-8 with a byte order mark, CRLF, a quoted cell with doubled quotes, a quoted cell holding ;, an empty row ;; and a discount printed the invoice to the cent at --rate 19 and 0%, exit 0; a heading row was refused with exit 2 and the message to save without it; the 62 tests pass. Nothing to mend.

Wrote the Made in rounds/invoicer/3/made.json: where each of the 9 decisions and the 4 Mores kept land, and 5 points settled with their grounds; it says that the 8 tracked compiled files are not yet untracked.

Ends with lacks: untracking the 8 compiled files under invoicer/__pycache__ and tests/__pycache__ needs git rm --cached (or deleting them), which no command allowed to the generator does; everything else is made, tried, and in the Made.

Updated the Made: invoicer N4 compiled files is carried out by .gitignore leaving __pycache__/ out and by fcb2254, which the main conversation made to untrack the 8 compiled files; 86581a1 is not in the branch history, as the main conversation checked. A rate of 0 prints Tax 0.00, tried in a throwaway copy.
Ends with done: every decision of the Cut is carried out, the compiled files by .gitignore and fcb2254, and the Made says where.
